title: DDL Triggers
description: Learn how to create DDL triggers to monitor and respond to schema changes.

data.text: DDL triggers respond to server or database events rather than to table data modifications. They fire in response to CREATE, ALTER, DROP, GRANT, DENY, REVOKE, or UPDATE STATISTICS statements.

data.title: CREATE DDL TRIGGER syntax
data.content: Creates a DDL trigger that fires on index-related events.

data.title: Track index changes with a DDL trigger
data.content: Creates a DDL trigger that logs index changes to a table.
data.code:
CREATE TRIGGER trg_index_changes
ON DATABASE
FOR
    CREATE_INDEX,
    ALTER_INDEX,
    DROP_INDEX
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    INSERT INTO index_logs (event_data, changed_by)
    VALUES (EVENTDATA(), USER);
END;

data.title: DDL Trigger Key Points
points: DDL triggers respond to schema definition changes, not data modifications.
They can be scoped to DATABASE or ALL SERVER.
Use EVENTDATA() to get information about the DDL event.
DDL triggers are useful for auditing schema changes and preventing unauthorized modifications.
